_comment: PocketTerm35 button map, captured on hardware over two independent passes.
This file is REFERENCE DATA, not runtime configuration. LinuxTouch does not
read evdev at all: global navigation is bound at the compositor level in
wm/sway/config, using the X keysyms in the 'keysym' field below. The file is
here because the mapping is the single most important fact about this
hardware, and because tools/capture_keymap.py regenerates it after an RP2040
The device presents a USB HID keyboard + mouse + consumer-control. There is
NO gamepad collection, so nothing here can arrive as a joystick event. The
D-pad is the real arrow cluster and L/R are the letter keys L and R -- there
'character': true means the key types a letter, and therefore MUST NOT be
bound globally. Only start and select are safe, which is the entire basis of
Do not hardcode the event device number. The keyboard was event0 on one card
and event1 on another; allocation order is not identity.
